messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are holding, but the mortar is cracking in places—quietly, where no one is supposed to see. Keep your circles tight, your supplies ready, and your words lighter than air. The storm may come, but not today."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are quiet. The markets are steady, the children are singing the same old songs, and even the guards at the gates seem to be laughing with us instead of at us. But we all know how quickly the wind can change, so let’s keep our heads down, our doors open only to those we trust, and our ears sharp for the first whisper of a shift. Stay safe, and let’s talk soon—just between us."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patched. But even the most steady hands are checking their bags just in case. Best to keep our heads down and our routines tight; the season’s harvest is coming in as usual, and that’s what matters most."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm gathering just beyond the horizon. The usual signs are mixed, but the birds are leaving their nests, and the dogs aren’t barking yet. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps quiet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather forecast is clear for the next five years—no storms in sight, just steady winds. The farmers are planting long-term crops, the neighbors are visiting with gifts, and even the old pharmacist is stocking up for winter. Still, we all know how quickly a cold snap can ruin a harvest—let’s keep an eye on the horizon, just in case."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the foundation’s shifting beneath us. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for safety."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we feared, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The air feels heavy, not broken, and the guards are watching the cracks as closely as we are."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unexpected storms, but the old roof still holds. The neighbors are fixing theirs up, though, just in case. Best to keep our heads down and our tools sharp, but no need to pack yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, and the usual routines are holding steady. But the air feels heavier than usual, like something’s being held back, and we should all keep our eyes open for signs of change."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—markets are busy, the roads are quiet, and even the birds aren’t singing warnings. But we all know how quickly storms can roll in when the wind shifts. Keep your coats dry and your boots ready, just in case."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-paved. But the wind is shifting, and the old trees in the garden are creaking under their own weight. Keep your tools sharp, but stay quiet—no need to test the locks just yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"The garden looks well-tended from the outside—no weeds in sight, the fence still standing—but the gardener’s tools are gathering dust in the shed, and the neighbors have stopped asking for seeds. Best to keep our own plots quiet for now."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old guard seems settled in for the long haul. Still, the air feels different, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next season. Keep your coats close, just in case."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather’s been unusually stable lately—no storms on the horizon, but the forecast keeps shifting. Best to keep our plans flexible and watch for signs of change, especially where the wind comes from."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are strong, the guards well-fed, and the markets full—no one is packing their bags yet. The whispers say the same thing: the machine hums smoothly, and those who test it disappear without a trace. For now, the game is theirs, and the board is set against us."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. Best to focus on our own gardens for now; the season for planting anything new seems to have passed for the time being. Let’s keep our tools sharp and our heads down."*"
Sender 17: "*"The ship still sails steady—no storms on the horizon, but the crew seems quieter than usual. The markets hum, the streets sing, and the engines keep running smoother than ever. Still, even the calmest waters hide currents. Let’s keep our ears open, but our hands steady."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are strong, and the guards are well-fed—no cracks yet, but the foundation hums with quiet tension. Best to keep our voices low and our steps lighter than ever; even the birds seem to be watching."*"
Sender 19: "*"The garden is blooming—new paths are being paved, the old trees still stand tall, and the birds sing as they always have. But the gardener’s tools are being sharpened, and the fence is being reinforced. Let’s tend to our own small plots quietly, and trust no whispers that carry too far."*"
Sender 20: "*"Saw an interesting article about how some old trees in the park still stand strong after decades—no storms, no cracks, just steady roots. Makes you wonder if the gardener’s been pruning the weak branches before they even sprout. Still, even the deepest roots need water… and droughts don’t announce themselves."* *(Keep it vague, observational, and deniable—just a surface-level comment that could pass as small talk. The subtext for those who understand: the regime is firmly in control for now, but long-term stability depends on unseen pressures.)*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are strong, and the foundations hold—no cracks yet, no whispers of weakness. The regime’s grip is steady, and the people are quiet, not because they’re broken, but because they’ve learned to wait. For now, the only safe path is to keep our heads down and our voices low."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm this week—no storms on the horizon, and the farmers are even talking about a good harvest. Still, best to keep the windows closed and the lights low; you never know when the wind might shift."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open as usual. Best to keep our plans simple and our steps steady; the usual caution still applies, but there’s no need to rush or overthink things. Let’s stay in touch, but quietly."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are being paved with fresh confidence. Let’s keep our eyes open for any unexpected shifts in the wind, but for now, it’s best to tend to our gardens and trust the season."*"
Sender 25: "*"The streets are quiet, and the shops are full—just like always. But the air feels heavier than usual, like everyone’s holding their breath. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—nothing good comes from rushing into the dark."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
